text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Peace Call signatories to hold rally in Algiers on March 14. The authorities had banned previous such attempts by Peace Call activists, who are seeking negotiations between the opposition and government to end Algeria's violence before a general election is held.
- Authorities arrest 20 people suspected of carrying out bomb attacks in Blida in February. Six more suspects on the run.
- Algeria's proportional voting system steers political parties to seek alliances to win seats in the parliament to be elected on June 5.
- State-enhanced housing sector achieved breakthrough in 1996 with 30,000 new houses built by individuals backed by government subsidy.
- Constitutionl council finds four articles in the newly voted party law as unconstitutional, including one over original Algerian nationality required for would-be party founders.
- Retirement fund owes the state over 17 billion dinars ($303 million).
- The Algerian Renewal Party to field candidates in the country's 372 constituencies.
- Leadership for the independent committee to oversee elections will be known tomorrow.
- Algeria is in better position to bargain terms of its deal with the European Union. Talks with the 15-nation bloc will resume next month in Algiers.
